new_statements.rule_in_words: Bisu is a three-tone register language (low/mid/high; Vacharee 1987 as cited by Person 2000: 36; Nishida 1973: 57-58 gives 55/33/11). Person states only that stress exists and is 'a relatively minor component' of the phonology; no source opened gives a placement rule. The only prominence asymmetry described is Nishida 1973: 59-60 — 'subordinate morphemes following another syllable have a specific tone when they are pronounced carefully, but in normal pronunciation, so-called weak utterances are observed', and 'main syllable + secondary syllable (/la, lə, lɯ, kha/ etc.) + the bound morpheme /-ŋe/' sequences show tone modulation — i.e. reduced (tonally weakened) secondary/bound syllables next to a full main syllable, not a word-stress rule.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None; Person 2000 gives no rule at all. Person 2000: 67-68 says Vacharee Nuamkaew's 1987 Mahidol thesis (Pha Daeng dialect) 'presents helpful information about syllable type, stress patterns, and phoneme distribution' — that thesis is the primary source for Bisu stress and could not be opened.
new_statements.domain_note: Person's remark is about syllable structure of the word; Nishida's weakening is a careful-vs-normal speech (phrase-level) phenomenon affecting bound morphemes and secondary syllables. Tone sandhi in verb phrases and particle clusters (Person 2000: 37) is the main suprasegmental process described.
new_statements.identity_note: Person 2000 describes the Thai Bisu of Doi Chomphuu (Amphoe Mae Lao) and Doi Pui (Amphoe Muang), Chiang Rai — the same village Nishida 1966/1973 calls Ban Lua Bisu of Ban Huai San and Bradley calls Huai Chomphu. Kitjapol 2006 Bisu data = Doi Chomphuu. Xu 1998/2001 (not opened) describe the Chinese Bisu (Laomian/Laopin) of Lancang County, Yunnan, which Person 2000: 68 says differs significantly from Thai Bisu. All fall under glottocode bisu1244 (no sub-dialect glottocodes).

new_statements.quote: §7 PROSODIE. "La courbe mélodique de la phrase Bisu se caractérise par une accentuation sur la syllabe finale des groupes syntaxiques, le Prédicat portant l'accentuation principale. En finale de phrase, on remarque une descente accentuelle." (p. 58) — §1 "La syllabe minimale en Bisu a la structure suivante Syllabe = Consonne + Voyelle + Ton [...] La structure de la syllabe théorique est donc: C + (C) + V + T + (C)" (p. 37) — §5.4 "Un lexème autonome peut cependant être créé par l'affixation de plusieurs lexèmes avec une variation tonale sur le dernier (élévation du ton résultant d'une accentuation à valeur morphologique)." (p. 58) — p. 78 "A l'initiale de phrase, en position Sujet, le pronom personnel porte l'accentuation normale du Prédicat. Ex : \"Je vais au marché\" / ga kátⁿɛ́ŋ / → [ ˈga kátⁿɛ́ŋ ]" — Tome 2 p. 3 "Les mots à préfixe [ ɑŋ- ] sont classés d'après l'initiale de la syllabe (accentuée) qui suit."
new_statements.translation: §7 PROSODY. "The melodic curve of the Bisu sentence is characterised by an accentuation on the final syllable of the syntactic groups, the Predicate carrying the main accentuation. At the end of the sentence one notices an accentual descent." — §1 "The minimal syllable in Bisu has the following structure: Syllable = Consonant + Vowel + Tone [...] The theoretical syllable structure is therefore C + (C) + V + T + (C)." — §5.4 "An autonomous lexeme can however be created by affixing several lexemes with a tonal variation on the last one (raising of the tone resulting from an accentuation with morphological value)." — p. 78 "At the beginning of the sentence, in Subject position, the personal pronoun carries the normal accentuation of the Predicate. Ex. 'I am going to the market' /ga kátⁿɛ́ŋ/ → [ˈga kátⁿɛ́ŋ]" — Tome 2 p. 3 "Words with the prefix [ɑŋ-] are filed according to the initial of the (accented) syllable that follows."

new_statements.relation_note: Compatible with the existing statement from Person 2000 (tone obligatory; stress 'a relatively minor component' with no placement rule): Beaudouin likewise gives no word-stress placement, but adds that the audible accentuation is phrase-final (group-final, predicate-main, sentence-final drop), that the prefix ɑŋ- is unaccented relative to the following root syllable, and that compound-final 'accentuation' surfaces as tone raising. The catalog record for Bisu has an empty rule; this source supports keeping it as tone-language with phrase-level accent only, no lexical stress rule.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bisu is a three-tone language (high/mid/low; tone is an obligatory constituent of every syllable, C+(C)+V+T+(C)). Beaudouin gives no word-level stress rule: the only accentuation he describes is phrase-level (final syllable of each syntactic group, strongest on the predicate, falling at sentence end), plus two lexical-domain remarks: in compounds the final element's tone is raised, which he attributes to a morphological accentuation, and the nominal/adjectival prefix ɑŋ- is treated as unaccented, the following root syllable as accented (Tome 2 p. 3). A sentence-initial subject pronoun takes the predicate's accentuation ([ˈga kátⁿɛ́ŋ]). He also notes that accent/tone interference is very rare (p. 140) and that exclamative particles are reinforced by an accentuation he transcribes as high tone (p. 107).
new_statements.exceptions: Prosodic analysis of read/translated texts is said to be unrepresentative of spontaneous speech (p. 140); the compound-final tone raising (e.g. tsɔ̀ŋkɔ̀ŋ 'forest' + wà 'pig' → tsɔ̀ŋkɔ̀ŋwá 'wild boar') is the one segment where 'accentuation' has a lexical effect, and it is realised as tone, not as a separate stress.
new_statements.identity_note: Beaudouin's reference dialect is Ban Doy (Huai Chomphu, 'Ban Lua'), Chiang Rai — the same Doi Chomphuu variety Person 2000 and Nishida 1973 describe; §8 (pp. 59-63) adds comparative notes on the Ban Ta Ko, Ban Pha Daeng and Ban Pwi Kham villages (segmental differences only, no prosodic differences reported).

tone_statements.quote: ภาษาบีซูเป็นภาษาที่มีระบบเสียงวรรณยุกต์ทำหน้าที่เป็นหน่วยทางภาษาเพื่อแยกความหมายของคำ [...] ผู้วิจัยพบว่า คำศัพท์ที่ใช้เก็บข้อมูลทั้ง 500 หน่วยอรรถ ปรากฏเสียงวรรณยุกต์ของภาษาบีซูทั้งหมด 3 หน่วยเสียง และพบหน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่เกิดการพัฒนาใหม่ 1 หน่วยเสียง ดังนี้ หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 1 เสียงกลาง เป็นวรรณยุกต์เดิมของภาษาบีซู คล้ายกับวรรณยุกต์สามัญ ในภาษาไทยมาตรฐาน หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 2 เสียงต่ำ เป็นวรรณยุกต์เดิมของภาษาบีซู [...] หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 3 วรรณยุกต์กลาง-ขึ้น เป็นวรรณยุกต์เดิมของภาษาบีซู [...] [p. 80] หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 4 วรรณยุกต์ตก คือ เสียงวรรณยุกต์โท ในภาษาไทยมาตรฐาน เป็นหน่วยเสียงที่ได้รับอิทธิพลจากปัจจัยภายนอก กล่าวคือได้รับอิทธิจากภาษาไทยมาตรฐาน
tone_statements.translation: Bisu is a language with a tone system that functions as a linguistic unit distinguishing word meanings [...] The researcher found that, across the 500-item wordlist used for data collection, three tonemes of Bisu appear in all, plus one newly developed toneme, as follows: Toneme 1, mid, is an original Bisu tone, similar to the Standard Thai mid (saman) tone; Toneme 2, low, is an original Bisu tone [similar to the Standard Thai low (ek) tone]; Toneme 3, mid-rising, is an original Bisu tone [similar to the Standard Thai high (tri) tone]; [p. 80] Toneme 4, falling, i.e. the Standard Thai falling (tho) tone, is a phoneme that has arisen under the influence of external factors, namely influence from Standard Thai.

tone_statements.citation: Person, Kirk R. 2007. A preliminary phonological sketch of Pyen, with comparison to Bisu. In Iwasaki Shoichi et al. (eds.), SEALS XIII: Papers from the 13th Annual Meeting of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society 2003, 193-201. Canberra: Pacific Linguistics, Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, The Australian National University.
tone_statements.quote: Pyen and Bisu have three contrastive tones, low, mid, and high, as illustrated in the following words (Vatcharee 1987: 110): ... hjá hjá hill field / hja hja chicken / hjà hjà to itch ... Vacharee’s analysis of 1,512 major syllables in Bisu found 422 low–tone syllables, 1,008 mid–tone syllables, and a mere 82 high–tone syllables (1987:115). This dramatic distribution curve accounts for the dearth of examples of three–way tonal contrast in the native lexicons of both Bisu and Pyen.
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (low, mid, high); tone obligatory in every native syllable (Sec. 2, p. 194). Triplet and tone-frequency counts credited to Vacharee 1987; fn. 8: Bisu writers confuse mid and low.

tone_statements.citation: Person, Kirk R. 2001. Writing Bisu: a community-based approach to orthography development. In Graham W. Thurgood (ed.), Papers from the Ninth Annual Meeting of the Southeast Asian Linguistics Society (1999), 171-200. Tempe: Arizona State University, Program for Southeast Asian Studies.
tone_statements.quote: As mentioned in section 5.1.2, there are three tones in Bisu: high, mid, and low. While minimal triads illustrating this contrast in identical environments are somewhat rare, rules of analogous contrast do seem to apply. ... Vacharee’s analysis of 1512 major syllables found 422 high tone syllables, 1008 mid tone syllables, and a mere 82 high tone syllables (Vacharee 1987). The orthography workshop participants initially decided to employ “middle” and “low” consonants ... resulting in a default mid tone with low and high tones marked maj eek ... or maj too ... respectively.
tone_statements.locator: p. 193, section 5.4 Tones; Table 12 'Tones' (field / chicken / to itch) on the same page; 5.1.2 p. 180 repeats 'Bisu has only three tones'
tone_statements.summary: Three level tones (high, mid, low) with a minimal triad; limited tone sandhi (5.5: negative ba lowers a following tone); '82 high tone syllables' is the source's slip for low. Forms count is a floor.

tone_statements.translation: 9) Since the consonant correspondence rules have already been set up and their common forms inferred, from here on the common form of a morpheme is shown with *. Note that the toneme correspondences follow this principle: Bisu high-level type (á) : Akha high-level type (á) : Bur. low-level type (a) / [Bisu] mid-level type (a) : [Akha] mid-level type (a) : [Bur.] high-falling type (a³), -V stop syllable / [Bisu] low-level type (à) : [Akha] low-level type (à) : [Bur.] high-level type (a²), -V stop syllable.
tone_statements.summary: Three level tonemes (high á, mid unmarked, low à) given as a correspondence key in a comparative paper; Part I p.457, fn.14: Bisu phɯ̀- 'tie' vs phɯ́- 'untie' toneme contrast judged old. 18+ forms.

sources.quote: ภาษาบีซูเป็นภาษาที่มีระบบเสียงวรรณยุกต์ทำหน้าที่เป็นหน่วยทางภาษาเพื่อแยกความหมายของคำ [...] ผู้วิจัยพบว่า คำศัพท์ที่ใช้เก็บข้อมูลทั้ง 500 หน่วยอรรถ ปรากฏเสียงวรรณยุกต์ของภาษาบีซูทั้งหมด 3 หน่วยเสียง และพบหน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่เกิดการพัฒนาใหม่ 1 หน่วยเสียง ดังนี้ หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 1 เสียงกลาง เป็นวรรณยุกต์เดิมของภาษาบีซู คล้ายกับวรรณยุกต์สามัญ ในภาษาไทยมาตรฐาน หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 2 เสียงต่ำ เป็นวรรณยุกต์เดิมของภาษาบีซู [...] หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 3 วรรณยุกต์กลาง-ขึ้น เป็นวรรณยุกต์เดิมของภาษาบีซู [...] [p. 80] หน่วยเสียงวรรณยุกต์ที่ 4 วรรณยุกต์ตก คือ เสียงวรรณยุกต์โท ในภาษาไทยมาตรฐาน เป็นหน่วยเสียงที่ได้รับอิทธิพลจากปัจจัยภายนอก กล่าวคือได้รับอิทธิจากภาษาไทยมาตรฐาน

sources.note: First-hand Pike-style phonemic analysis of a 500-item list from 15 Doi Chomphu speakers in three age groups: Bisu is a tone language with three native tonemes, T1 mid, T2 low, T3 mid-rising, plus a fourth, falling tone (like Standard Thai tho) that is attributed to Standard Thai influence and is not natively contrastive ('no minimal-pair contrast in the language', p. 80); it surfaces in Thai loans and as a variant of native tones (T2 > T4 mostly in age group 3; in a few native words such as 'rainbow', 'spider' even some age-group-1 speakers use T4, p. 83, table 4.41). Variation T1>T2, T1>T3,…

tone.translation: Bisu is a language with a tone system that functions as a linguistic unit distinguishing word meanings [...] The researcher found that, across the 500-item wordlist used for data collection, three tonemes of Bisu appear in all, plus one newly developed toneme, as follows: Toneme 1, mid, is an original Bisu tone, similar to the Standard Thai mid (saman) tone; Toneme 2, low, is an original Bisu tone [similar to the Standard Thai low (ek) tone]; Toneme 3, mid-rising, is an original Bisu tone [similar to the Standard Thai high (tri) tone]; [p. 80] Toneme 4, falling, i.e. the Standard Thai falling (tho) tone, is a phoneme that has arisen under the influence of external factors, namely influence from Standard Thai.

sources.quote: Pyen and Bisu have three contrastive tones, low, mid, and high, as illustrated in the following words (Vatcharee 1987: 110): ... hjá hjá hill field / hja hja chicken / hjà hjà to itch ... Vacharee’s analysis of 1,512 major syllables in Bisu found 422 low–tone syllables, 1,008 mid–tone syllables, and a mere 82 high–tone syllables (1987:115). This dramatic distribution curve accounts for the dearth of examples of three–way tonal contrast in the native lexicons of both Bisu and Pyen.
sources.note: Three level tones (low, mid, high); tone obligatory in every native syllable (Sec. 2, p. 194). Triplet and tone-frequency counts credited to Vacharee 1987; fn. 8: Bisu writers confuse mid and low.

sources.quote: As mentioned in section 5.1.2, there are three tones in Bisu: high, mid, and low. While minimal triads illustrating this contrast in identical environments are somewhat rare, rules of analogous contrast do seem to apply. ... Vacharee’s analysis of 1512 major syllables found 422 high tone syllables, 1008 mid tone syllables, and a mere 82 high tone syllables (Vacharee 1987). The orthography workshop participants initially decided to employ “middle” and “low” consonants ... resulting in a default mid tone with low and high tones marked maj eek ... or maj too ... respectively.

sources.note: Three level tones (high, mid, low) with a minimal triad; limited tone sandhi (5.5: negative ba lowers a following tone); '82 high tone syllables' is the source's slip for low. Forms count is a floor.

sources.note: Confirms the catalog classification tonal and supplies the tone inventory the catalog rule leaves empty: three tones, high / mid / low (Beaudouin data) or high level / mid level / low level-or-low-falling (Nishida data). Tone is marked on the syllable (canon 'T C(C)V(C)'). The work says nothing about stress for Bisu, so it neither supports nor contradicts the 'tone-and-stress' class; secondary stress, weight, domain and exceptions are not mentioned. Not first-hand: a compiled inventory from Beaudouin 1988 (Glossary) / 1991 (Une monographie du Bisu, pp. 39-94) and Nishida 1966 via Bradley 1979…

tone.translation: 9) Since the consonant correspondence rules have already been set up and their common forms inferred, from here on the common form of a morpheme is shown with *. Note that the toneme correspondences follow this principle: Bisu high-level type (á) : Akha high-level type (á) : Bur. low-level type (a) / [Bisu] mid-level type (a) : [Akha] mid-level type (a) : [Bur.] high-falling type (a³), -V stop syllable / [Bisu] low-level type (à) : [Akha] low-level type (à) : [Bur.] high-level type (a²), -V stop syllable.
